episodes.title: The Fast Breeder Reactor
sources: Department of Atomic Energy / PIB, 4 March 2024: commencement of core loading at the 500 MWe Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor, Kalpakkam, built by BHAVINI; the PFBR uses U-Pu mixed oxide fuel and a U-238 blanket; will produce more fuel than it consumes; second stage of the three-stage programme
Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR) pages: sodium-cooled fast reactors; breeding of Pu-239 from U-238; later use of thorium to breed U-233
NCERT Class 12 Physics, ch. 13 (Nuclei): nuclear fission, chain reaction, moderators

options: More fissile fuel than it uses
quiz.why: It turns uranium-238 into plutonium-239: new fuel.

quiz.q: What cools a fast breeder reactor?
quiz.why: Water would slow the neutrons; sodium keeps them fast.
The 500 MW PFBR is at Kalpakkam, Tamil Nadu.

review.note: Facts were read against the DAE/PIB release of 4 March 2024 and IGCAR's pages. No photo of the plant; diagrams only. Moving facts: the reactor's later milestones (criticality, power) are not stated; check before re-using.

episodes.title: India's Three-Stage Nuclear Plan
sources: Department of Atomic Energy, 'Three Stage Nuclear Power Programme' (dae.gov.in): stage 1 PHWRs on natural uranium; stage 2 fast breeder reactors on plutonium, U-238 and later thorium blankets; stage 3 thorium/U-233 reactors; formulated by Homi Bhabha in the 1950s
DAE / PIB, 4 March 2024: core loading began at the 500 MWe Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor, Kalpakkam
DAE / Atomic Minerals Directorate: India's thorium is in monazite in coastal beach sands; among the world's largest thorium resources

quiz.q: Why does India's plan centre on thorium?
options: India has large thorium and small uranium reserves
quiz.why: India has a great deal of thorium in beach sands, but little uranium.

quiz.q: Which reactors make up stage one?
quiz.why: Stage one uses natural uranium in heavy water reactors.

quiz.q: What must thorium become before it can fuel a reactor?
quiz.why: Thorium is bred into uranium-233 first.

review.note: Facts were read against DAE's page on the three-stage programme and the PIB release of 4 March 2024. Diagrams only. Moving facts: stage-two milestones after core loading are not stated; check before re-using.

episodes.title: The Repo Rate in 60 Seconds
sources: RBI, 'Monetary Policy' and FAQ on the Liquidity Adjustment Facility (rbi.org.in): repo rate as the policy rate; collateralised by government securities; Marginal Standing Facility as the upper bound; Standing Deposit Facility as the floor of the corridor since April 2022
RBI Act, 1934, section 45ZI: MPC decisions by majority; Governor has a casting vote in a tie; at least four meetings a year (in practice six)
NCERT Class 12 Macroeconomics, ch. 3: tools of monetary policy

quiz.q: The repo rate is the rate at which…
options: The RBI lends to banks against securities
quiz.why: Banks borrow from the RBI, giving bonds as security.

quiz.q: Which is the floor of the RBI's rate corridor today?
quiz.why: The SDF replaced the fixed-rate reverse repo as the floor in April 2022.

quiz.q: If the MPC vote is tied, who decides?
quiz.why: The Governor has a casting vote.

review.note: Facts were read against RBI's monetary policy pages and the RBI Act. The corridor bars are relative positions, not rates. Moving facts: the actual repo rate is deliberately not stated; it changes.

episodes.title: How GST Taxes Only the Value Added
sources: The Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016: Article 246A, Article 269A and Article 279A (GST Council: Union Finance Minister as chairperson, state finance ministers as members)
CBIC, GST concept and status / FAQs (cbic-gst.gov.in): GST rolled out 1 July 2017; destination-based tax on supply; input tax credit removes the cascading effect
The worked example uses an imaginary 10% rate for arithmetic only

quiz.q: What does input tax credit prevent?
quiz.why: Each seller subtracts tax already paid.

quiz.q: Which Article creates the GST Council?

review.note: Facts were read against the 101st Amendment Act and CBIC's GST pages. The 10% example is labelled as imaginary in the narration. Moving facts: GST rate slabs change; none are stated.
